svg.text: NEXUS - STM32 carrier and 5 V split board: soldering and wiring

Kit perfboards (BOM 5.11), 2.54 grid · Board A 5×7 cm (18 × 24 holes) under CN10, board B 3×7 cm (10 × 24) under CN7 of the NUCLEO-H533RE, 26 mm apart · Board C 3×7 cm (10 × 24), the 5 V split · MEC-08 / MEC-15 / HW-19

Hole names: board·hole, as PRINTED on the kit board - on A (5×7) letters A-X along the 70 mm side and numbers 1-18 across, on B and C (3×7) numbers 1-24 along and letters A-J across; A1 bottom-left with the print readable, as every view shows it.

Nucleo header row k sits on B's hole row k + 5 and A's k + 4 (A one pitch ahead, the tray) · CN10 even pins A·B12-T12, odd B11-T11 · CN7 even B·J1-J19, odd I1-I19 · fixings: the corner holes, three on B (MEC-17).

Wires on the solder side, ALL INSULATED. On A and B no wire goes on a pin: it lands on the free hole beside it, one wire per hole, and a solder bridge (silver) joins the two. Only B's two ringed CN7 pins (E5V, 3V3) take the wire straight. Thick 18 AWG (3.11), thin 22 AWG.

The socket carries its own 5.1k Rd on CC1 and CC2 (4.98k measured, 2026-10-07). Its CC wires are cut short and insulated: the FRDM boots on VBUS and GND alone.
The USB-C body rides 2.5 mm up on its flange. Ties through 3 mm holes at I2 / B2 and I6 / B6, the second one over the pigtail.

Nothing is drilled in the boards. The tray (MEC-17) takes them from below; only the tray is screwed to plate 2 (T1-T6).
One hole is drilled in the tray by hand, for B's rear inboard corner, at plate 2 (187.03, 83.65).
A·X.. at chassis x 181.20, B·X.. at x 183.74 · Nucleo row 1 at x 171.04, its outline x 120.2-202.7 · A y 5.11, B y 111.15.
ORIENTATION - where A and B sit under the Nucleo
Nucleo from above, components up, as in every view.
CN1, the ST-LINK USB-C, points to the REAR (fascia).
CN10 is the header on the vehicle RIGHT: board A goes under it.
CN7 is the header on the vehicle LEFT: board B goes under it.
Both have pin 1 (yellow) at the CN1 end, in their vehicle-LEFT column.
Red triangle = the corner at printed hole A1.
On A and on B: the FRONT corner on the vehicle-LEFT edge.
Mark that corner on both faces with a pen before soldering:
both boards then read the same way up, print legible.
CHECK BEFORE THE IRON IS HOT
1 Count the holes: A needs 18 × 24, B and C 10 × 24. The drawing assumes the usual kit counts; a board one row short moves everything.
2 New A and B: A on the last 5×7, B on a 3×7. Cut four 1×19 strips from the 40-pin female headers and dry-fit them on the Nucleo, A and B
screwed to the tray under it: A·B12-T12 / B11-T11 and B·J1-J19 / I1-I19. Nothing else goes in the columns under the Nucleo.
3 Solder the sockets WITH THE NUCLEO PLUGGED IN and A and B screwed to the tray: it sets the 63.50 mm between the rows. Tack two corners, check, finish.
4 SN65HVD230 FACE DOWN on A, as bent: sockets A·H18-H15 = CTX, CRX, GND, 3V3, and
A·O17 / O16 = CANH / CANL, 7 holes behind. Its screw terminal is unused. CANH-CANL unpowered must read ~120 Ω: keep its terminator (HW-09).
5 The kit terminals may be 5.0 mm, not 5.08: the 3p CAN block spans 10.0 vs 10.16 mm of holes. Push it in; do not drill.
6 Before the Nucleo goes in: 5 V to GND not shorted · 6 V isolated from 5 V and 3V3 · 5 V on B·J17 (E5V) only, nothing on J11 (5V) or I17 (VDD) · JP5 on [5-6].
7 Fixings: nothing is drilled in the boards. An 8 mm nylon standoff and a screw in each corner hole of A and C and three of B; drill the tray
for B's rear inboard one (MEC-17). No wire may pass under a standoff. Nothing is fitted on the solder side: it carries wires only.
8 The two I2C headers are 90° headers on A along the gap, pins pointing forward; nothing may stand where their plugs lie (violet). Plug both before the Nucleo.
9 Bridges before wires: run each silver bridge from the pin onto its free hole(s), then lay the wire end on that hole. Meter every bridge to its neighbours.
Why A and B split this way
New boards on the same tray (MEC-17). Every CAN pin is on
CN10 and every supply pin on CN7, so A takes CAN and I2C and B the
power and the servo (PA15): one wire crosses, 3V3. Each header is
in its module's order: a straight lead is right.
Both 470 µF caps and every resistor are now on a board. C2 sits at
the servo header, where the stall current is. C1 is on board C,
which is the 5 V split: the FRDM's amps never cross the STM32
carrier. No Rp is fitted: the FRDM boots on plain 5 V (HW-02).
The carrier's one ground lead is B 5V IN GND, back through C to the
(−) WAGO (HW-06). The 6 V servo rail reaches C2 and SERVO only
(HW-11). 3V3 comes from CN7-16, the Nucleo's own regulator, never
CN7-5 VDD. 5 V enters on E5V, so the ST-LINK USB alone does not
power the MCU: LOGIC on first, then the USB. R4 guards PA15.

Geometry: UM3121 Fig. 7 (board 70 × 82.5, outer rows 63.50 apart, 3.25 in from each edge, row 1 31.70 from the CN1 edge) · Pins: UM3121 Table 17 · AFs: DS14539 Rev 3 (PB12 / PB13 AF9, PB6 / PB7 AF4, PA15 AF1)
Decisions: MEC-08 (carrier) · MEC-15 (kit boards) · HW-19 (5 V split board, selectable termination) · HW-06 · HW-09 · HW-11 · HW-18 · SVG is the master - PDFs are generated once the design is frozen.
